anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers the Change cleanly: the initial numeric 2 persists course deliver and caps 10/10 before writes, P1 and CI-minted P2 are repaired across waves with closure review and no intermediate menu, own pushes renew the deadline (12:17, 12:25, 12:27) while the 12:11 base-only observation is explicitly marked as not renewing, BEHIND queues the sync without a pick, and final offers merge but stops on the new numeric 2. B keeps the repeated-red/no-source-change exit and names the base sync as non-qualifying, C watches the in-progress re-run with P1 retained and resolves via fresh claim check with no extra dispatch or spent round, and D now separates repair.wave.sync.pre_head B from expected_remote_head A (Before conflated pre_head with the remote lease, which is why f6 moved). Nothing regressed relative to Before. Two small hardening suggestions: in the main-sequence table say 'fresh helper' explicitly for the P1 and P2 waves rather than leaving it implied by the digest, and in D state outright that pre_head and expected_remote_head are persisted before the rebase begins, so the ordering claim is in the text rather than inferred from row order.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before refused the whole entry (deliver treated as an unsupported verb), so it never repaired P1/P2, never pushed, never synced, never watched C's re-run, and left D's local head at C with no persisted restore/lease heads; only f4 held there because its B row still recorded an exit and stated that a base sync is not a pushed repair-wave source commit. After delivers the Change cleanly: a single numeric 2 persists course deliver with 0/10 caps, the table carries the three own-push deadlines (12:17, 12:25, 12:27) and explicitly marks the 12:11 base observation as non-renewing, BEHIND queues the sync without a pick, final offers merge and stop executes nothing, B exits stuck on repeated red naming base-only SHA movement as insufficient, C admits the bounded watch of the one authorized re-run and reaches final with no further dispatch/re-run/round, and D records sync.pre_head B and expected_remote_head A, leases against A, and restores clean B with no second push. Nothing in After regressed a fact. Two wording nits that do not move facts but could confuse a reader: the main-sequence stop paragraph says it 'deletes the run record, helper outputs, captured logs' and then 'No ... terminal cleanup runs' — pick one phrasing (e.g. 'retires this PR's record/helper/log files; no branch deletion, base pull or merge consequence'); and in D, 'increment sync usage once before sync' sits in the Before-rewrite row while the table never shows the resulting syncs value, so showing the numeric usage column (e.g. 'syncs n→n+1') would make the independent-accounting claim verifiable at a glance.
